body.text: Mon, 14 Sept, 11:00 pm, Final score, ZIM 235, AUS 8/294
Pat Cummins live updates: Test cricket captain to address Usman Khawaja ball-tampering claims
Australia Test captain Pat Cummins is speaking to the media about Usman Khawaja's recent revelations about Australia's ball tampering in 2018.
Follow along in our live blog below, and watch live on ABC News Channel.

'Utter nonsense' that bowlers were the architects

"I think Usman actually says things that are far more serious than [ball tampering allegations]. He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense.

"I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out Usman admitted he told Cam [Bancroft] to be careful when using sandpaper. That's not Usman that I know. It's not the Usman that has been part of the team that's helped rebuild the Australian cricket culture over the last eight years.
"The Usman I know would have stopped that from happening there and then."
Key Event
Usman '100 per cent wrong' saying they all knew: Cummins
"When he says 'we all knew', if that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100 per cent wrong.
"I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening."

'Only people with agendas want to keep this going': McGrath
In the world of roughly a million cricket podcasts, Australian bowling legend Glenn McGrath has had his say and he wants everyone to move on.
"No-one's saying what they did is not wrong. They were bloody idiots for what they did; they should never have done it," he said.

"I'm a big fan of leaving the past in the past, but learn from it. We're all custodians of this great game. What's the benefit to the game of cricket by wanting to find out all these answers? There is no benefit positively to the game of Test cricket.
"CA should come out [and say] 'We've dealt with that in the past, this is Usman's story, this is how he feels' and just leave it at that and move on."
McGrath says "it's only people with agendas that want this to keep going".

"Journalists love it because they've got stories to write. Other countries can use that against Australia, and journalists from other countries that didn't like Australia being so strong, they love it they will use it."
Speaking as a journalist from this country, I can't say I've had that much fun this week, but simply moving on from a massive scandal like this is a bit of an over-simplification.

As Usman Khawaja said, he was never spoken to as part of the investigation into Cape Town. It seems odd that any investigation wouldn't include speaking to, at the very least, all 11 players on the field at the time.
What's in Usman Khawaja's book?
A lot of people have been going off media reports with regards to what Usman Khawaja wrote in his book.
David Mark has read the thing and broken down the Sandpapergate chapters for you.
An odd process

If he maintains the bowler’s story of the past eight years he’s going to have to say Khawaja and Warner are lying. ‘Different views and memories ‘ isn’t going to wash. I can see this ending up in court if they’re not careful. - Phillip

Hi Phillip,
As far as why Cummins is doing this, he needed to front the media.
He's the captain of the Test team and was a member of the bowling unit in the 2018 series in South Africa.
The announcement of the media conference/gaggle/doorstop was peculiar though.

Normally we'd get an email from Cricket Australia's communications department saying something like: "Pat Cummins will be available to media from 9:30am AEDT at Cricket Central. Please arrive at 9:15am."
But Cummins's tweet that he's going to be doing some training and will speak after that and he'll "ask CA to send out details", was certainly a little strange.
Key Event
What can we expect from Pat Cummins?
Pat Cummins said yesterday he has "taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly".

Nothing wrong with wrapping your head around what's been said to avoid going off media reports, but in the meantime a lot of his past and present teammates have been doing media opps and been forced to answer questions about it.
The party line from current players has pretty much been: "Usman's told his story, which he's entitled to do, but I'm not keen to relitigate the events of 2018."
If that's all Cummins offers this morning, this could be a very frustrating morning for him and reporters.
When the prospect of Khawaja's book came out, Cummins revealed they had spoken ahead of time and the skipper said:

"It's obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times. It was dealt with then. All I can say is as a group we've moved on. [I'm] very happy with the last eight or nine years, how we've been as a group and evolved. He didn't go into too much detail … As always, it was, 'No worries. You can tell your story. That's fine.'"

The issue is, while Khawaja's book tells the story from his perspective, it's not only his story because it does implicate others. Whether that's saying an unnamed assistant coach called for more work on the ball, or implying an unnamed fast bowler knew more than has been let on, or shedding more light on the conduct of David Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, these are Khawaja's stories but they're ABOUT others.
Cummins was there and now, eight years later, he's the captain of this Test team. It would be good if we could have a few more answers than the usual, but I'm not overly optimistic to be honest.
Let us know your thoughts
As we wait for Pat Cummins, please chime into the comments to let us know your thoughts and ask your questions.

So, in between a training session and the start of play on day three between New South Wales and South Australia, the Australian men's Test captain will speak to reporters about ball tampering, sandpaper, Usman Khawaja etc.
He said he's going to speak at 9:30am AEDT.
Key Event
We're waiting to hear from Pat Cummins
Good morning and welcome to another day of rolling coverage of … the 2018 Cape Town Test match?
No, you've not fallen into a time vortex. Instead, Usman Khawaja's tell-a-lot book has reignited the conversation around Sandpapergate, ball tampering and Australia's actions all those years ago.
Today, the next chapter in the saga, as men's Test captain Pat Cummins fronts the media in Sydney.
We'll bring you every moment as it happens.
